newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger, spreads at 11-yr lows.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger, spreads at 11-yr lows.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Tuesday, with spreads to U.S. bonds reaching new 11-year lows, amid foreign buying and term-extension by domestic investors, analysts said.

"People are still very interested in Canada and the theme of spread compression," said Michael Gregory, an economist with Lehman Brothers. "Canada's very positive fundamentals are allowing yields to continue to do better than the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.00 to C$108.15 to yield 7.30 percent compared to the U.S. 30-year benchmark which rose 1/32 to yield 6.84 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 46, the lowest since 1985, from 55 basis points Friday's close.
"Overnight there was interest out of Europe and the U.S. today as well, so I think probably Europe, the U.S., and some term extension by domestic investors is all helping," said Gregory.

Canadian-U.S. bond spreads have narrowed sharply in the past two weeks with investors encouraged by the country's shrinking budget deficit, low inflation and first current account surplus in 12 years. Some analysts predict positive spreads at the 10-year portion level could soon vanish.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.80 to C$102.98 to yield 6.59 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark gained 1/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
The spread between the two shrank to an 11-year low of 4 basis points from 16 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.43 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.18 percent.
